messages:
rishi: saw a weird pattern tonight  — dedicated-eu2 pool got an extra 40GB/s of egress for ~6m and we hit p99 token latency across the rack. alert from netwatch: https://netwatch/redwood/alerts/2345

dana: omg that was us. a training job accidentally matched dedicated-eu2 selector due to a stale tenant-tag rule. migrating now.

miguel: can you paste the pod labels? we recently added tenant.stage=prod fallback to dedicated pools and it may have a catch-all.

dana: snippet: `kubectl get pods -l job=large-train -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.labels}'` -> `tenant:acme, tenant.stage:prod, model.family:decoder-x`

rishi: yeah fallback fired because tenant.stage=prod is in the dedicated pool affinity list. That was supposed to be `tenant.stage:prod-eligible` not just `prod`. human error.

infra-bot: ticket created: INFRA-7892 "dedicated pool selector mis-match - acme training job" assigned to dana

miguel: mitigation options: 1) cordon that dedicated-eu2 rack for prefill/low-priority allocations 2) apply a per-tenant egress cap via qdisc on the node 3) evict offending pods (graceful) and drain to best-effort pool

dana: trying option 3 first. running `podctl evict --selector job=large-train --grace 30s` now.

rishi: while we're evicting, can we patch the pool selector to be stricter? `poolctl patch dedicated-eu2 --selector 'tenant.stage in (prod-eligible)'` to prevent recurrence.

miguel: +1. also add a quick admission webhook check so label typos fail on create. I can spin up a small webhook in 10m.

infra-bot: eviction: 12 pods evicted from dedicated-eu2 at 1912345790 by dana  status: requeued to best-effort

dana: requeued ok, latency tail dropping already. 99th down from 480ms to 140ms in 2m. graphs: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/net/egress?var-region=eu2

rishi: cost note: those cross-pool requeues hit egress and also caused ~0.7% increase in billed inter-region transfer for the month so far. we'll need to notify finance if this pattern continues.

miguel: created PR to tighten selectors + admission check: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/5123

product-ops: heads-up for product teams: if you use tenant.stage label for routing, please follow the new naming convention `prod-eligible` vs `prod`. we'll send a short slack post with steps to migrate.

rishi: follow-ups: 1) dana to patch pool selector and deploy webhook (owner: dana) 2) miguel to add node-level egress qdisc as a safety net (owner: miguel) 3) infra to run a one-off audit of pools for permissive selectors (owner: rishi) 4) product-ops to broadcast label convention (owner: product-ops)

dana: on it. putting times: patch + webhook by EOD, qdisc proof-of-concept tomorrow AM.

miguel: qdisc plan: tc qdisc add dev eth0 root tbf rate 120mbit burst 64kb latency 50ms for cross-pool traffic only. need to test impact on low-latency inference.

rishi: good. we should also add a metric: pool-selector-permissiveness and alert if > 0.1% of new allocations match "fallback" selectors.

infra-bot: follow-up reminder scheduled: 1912422078 (24h) for INFRA-7892

dana: thanks all. lesson learned: selectors are safety-critical. will add a tiny test in CI to catch ambiguous selector additions.
